correctness.rationale: The two complete finite arithmetic implementations use different algorithms (curve-point/line incidence and independent quartic-root counting), verify every field inverse, enumerate all 532171 projective lines and centers, and agree on all 17 exterior fiber-count rows, 39879 four-secants, and the 63 F9 exceptional centers. Smoothness follows from projective partial derivatives, genus from adjunction, and the projection equivalence from a basepoint-free degree-four line pencil. Finite enumeration here is exhaustive, not a sample.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2022 Irsee slide explicitly establishes q=3,r=3 arc completeness and an on-curve incidence formula, so those weaker known claims are excluded. The 2023 Hermitian-arc article and 2025 sufficiently-large-q theorem do not state the full 17-value exterior completely split projection-fiber spectrum or the 63-point F9 maximal locus. Actual targeted published-finding corpus searches returned no dominating arithmetic distribution. Residual unindexed tables or original Magma data pose a stated originality risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed tables or unpublished original Magma results associated with the 2022 q=3 completeness calculation may already contain finer exterior incidences.
Published literature search is not an exhaustive novelty certificate.

value.rationale: Splitting of rational fibers of all degree-four projections from exterior centers of a natural smooth genus-three Hermitian quartic is a motivated arithmetic invariant. The 17-valued exact spectrum (in contrast to prior binary completeness), uniform minimum 25 and exceptional 63-point subfield locus give a complete natural classification with a geometric descent feature. No generalized theorem is required to make the exact distribution meaningful.
